theme: A material that remembers which way you came
title: Shape-Memory Strip — predicting a hysteresis loop across held-out paths
strategies: trivial: predict the constant mean training force, ignoring x and b entirely -> reproduces the checker's own constant baseline (~0.1)

greedy: memoryless symbolic regression y=f(x) (least-squares cubic in x, ignoring the branch variable b) -- fits the visible single loop reasonably since it captures the centerline trend, but the SAME x is visited by both the loading and unloading branch at different y, so no function of x alone can separate them; the unrecoverable branch-mixing error dominates on more agitated held-out paths

strong: the insight -- recognise the output is path-dependent, not a function of x alone. Derive the branch sequence b from the training x's directions (the fixed, stated rule), fit BOTH the centerline g(x) and the branch-modulated gap c(x) via least squares on features [1,x,x^2,x^3,b,b*x^2], and emit a closed-form expression that references b explicitly -- generalises across held-out paths with new reversal points and a different sampling rate

headroom above strong: model the fully exact planted cubic/quadratic shape (not just a truncated low-order fit) and account for the wider/extrapolated elongation range on the harder test ids; sensor noise keeps even the exact law off the ceiling
